clue.text: Little Boy Blue changing to clerical wear.

parts.note: Chas is a short form of Charles, a boy's name made little

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the word blue are rearranged

explanation.surface: The nursery-rhyme shepherd boy swaps his blue outfit for a priest's robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Boy Blue' reads as the nursery-rhyme character, but splits into a shortened name plus the anagram fodder; 'changing' turns BLUE into UBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is the sleeveless outer vestment a priest puts on to celebrate Mass, so it is clerical clothing.

clue.text: He 'included nothing overweight in his pictures:

definitions.text: He 'included nothing overweight in his pictures

indicators.note: included means the word He takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written
O is the round figure zero, nothing
lb is the abbreviation for a pound, a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A portrait painter took care never to show anyone fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts O and LB inside HE, then IN follows; the whole clue also describes the Tudor court painter, who painted the famously stout Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Holbein the Younger was a German-born painter of Tudor court portraits.

clue.text: The end of the 'Capulets could be 'conjecture

indicators.note: could be signals that the word Capulets can be rearranged into something else
The end of picks the last letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A theatregoer wonders how Juliet's family's story might finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges CAPULETS into SPECULAT; 'The end of the' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is to guess or form a theory without firm evidence.

clue.text: Maltreat a toad holed up in it?

definitions.text: a toad holed up in it?
definitions.meaning: toad-in-the-hole is a British dish of sausages baked in a flour-egg-milk mixture

explanation.definitionFit: To batter is to beat someone; batter is also the pudding mix that the sausages of toad-in-the-hole sit in.

clue.text: Anglo-French Concorde ? :

parts.note: not the supersonic airliner but agreement, concord, between Britain and France

explanation.surface: The supersonic jet built jointly by Britain and France.
explanation.walkthrough: Concorde suggests the aircraft, but the clue means harmony; the answer is the 1904 Anglo-French agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1904 agreement settling colonial disputes between Britain and France was called the friendly understanding, a diplomatic concord.

clue.text: Standard description of wine far out of this world

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in 'up to par'
sec is French for dry, the word printed on labels describing a dry wine

explanation.surface: A wine label's usual tasting note turns out to be far beyond earthly.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is an astronomical unit of distance, about 3.26 light years, used for stars far beyond our planet.

clue.text: "As you was before you were!"—such a state!

definitions.text: "As you was before you were!"—such a state!

parts.words: "As you was before you were!"—such a state!
parts.note: the parade-ground order 'As you were' twisted to mean the condition one was in before one existed, i.e. before birth

explanation.surface: A sergeant major bellows a garbled order to return to position.
explanation.definitionFit: Prenatal describes the condition of a baby before it is born.

clue.text: Sonny in school-—" sunny outside the church ?

indicators.note: outside means the sun word goes around the church abbreviation

parts.note: solar means of the sun
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A boy at school is out in the sunshine beyond the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sonny' is any young boy; one in school is a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar in the old sense is a schoolboy or pupil.

clue.text: 19 is about to ponder material

indicators.note: is about means the 19 answer goes round the other word

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, the sea substance from Ariel's song
to pore over something is to study or ponder it

explanation.surface: Someone is about to think over an answer and some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts PORE inside CORAL, the answer to 19.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily or physical, as opposed to spiritual.

clue.text: He gives warning about start of bombing

indicators.note: about means the warning word is placed around the other letter

parts.note: an alert is a warning, as in an air-raid alert

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the word bombing

explanation.surface: Someone sounds the air-raid warning as the bombing begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the whole definition: the answer is simply a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert is a man's name, so it can stand for any male person referred to as he.

clue.text: This man digging into the food on it

definitions.text: This man digging into the food on it

parts.words: This man digging into the food on it
parts.note: read one way, a man who digs trenches; read another, the wooden platter a hearty eater digs his food from

explanation.surface: A hungry diner tucks in to the meal on his plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencher is an old wooden serving board for food, and literally one who cuts trenches is a digger.

clue.text: Eastern nuclear explosion out of the blue

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A nuclear blast in the East comes suddenly, out of the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' rearranges E plus NUCLEAR; 'out of' is a link, and 'out of the blue' is a misleading idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerulean is a deep sky-coloured shade, so it names the blue of the heavens.

clue.text: Divine leader of nine

definitions.meaning: a divine as a noun is a god or deity
the nine Muses were led by the god of music and poetry

explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was a Greek god and, as Musagetes, the leader of the nine Muses.

clue.text: Grass snake swallows its tail

indicators.note: swallows means that end letter is taken back inside the word

parts.note: taken as written
the tail of the word snake is its last letter

explanation.surface: A snake in the grass eats its own tail, like the ancient ouroboros symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of SNAKE is moved inward, as if swallowed, to sit between N and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass is British slang for informing on someone, and to sneak means the same: to tell tales.

clue.text: Cup-supporter sees: players heading 'the table'

indicators.note: heading means the players word sits on top of the table word in this down entry

parts.note: a side is a team of players
board is an old word for a table, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: A football fan watches the players top the league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup-supporter' looks like a football fan; it is furniture holding crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a piece of dining-room furniture on which cups and dishes stand.

clue.text: Chaps go to Silver Lake to see animals there

parts.note: chaps are men
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Some men visit a silver lake to watch the wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a place visited: the collection of animals you go to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild creatures kept for exhibition, a place you visit to view beasts.

clue.text: Romantic match is made' to work in principle

definitions.text: Romantic match is made' to work in principle

parts.words: Romantic match is made' to work in principle
parts.note: a romantic couple runs off together so that their marriage can go ahead despite opposition

explanation.surface: A love match is arranged to function in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: An elopement is a secret running away by lovers to marry.

clue.text: The way 'to make enemies is, classically, to have a row

parts.note: est is Latin for is, Latin being a classical language
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Advice that the way to fall out with people is to start a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to turn people who were close into strangers or foes.

clue.text: Out-of-the-way pastime ?

definitions.meaning: a route that takes traffic off the usual road, a detour

explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is both a detour sending traffic a roundabout way and an amusement that diverts the mind.

clue.text: Jerome's work destroyed in glue vat.

indicators.note: destroyed signals that the words glue and vat are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholar's manuscript is ruined when it falls into a tub of adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vulgate is St Jerome's fourth-century Latin translation of the Bible.

clue.text: Made by bones at full fathom five

definitions.text: Made by bones at full fathom five

parts.words: Made by bones at full fathom five
parts.note: recalls Ariel's song in The Tempest, where the drowned father's bones lie five fathoms deep and are turned to a sea substance

explanation.surface: A drowned man's skeleton slowly becomes something new on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line 'Of his bones are coral made' describes the reef material formed at the bottom of the sea.

clue.text: Its 'capital" resurrected-from ashes

parts.note: the capital city is named after the mythical bird that rises again from its own ashes

explanation.surface: A city rebuilt after a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenix, named after the bird reborn from ashes, is the capital of this US state.

clue.text: What Rubinstein wrote in' the French capital

definitions.text: What Rubinstein wrote in' the French capital

parts.words: What Rubinstein wrote in' the French capital
parts.note: seemingly a work composed in Paris, but the French capital letter is F, the key of the composer's famous piano piece

explanation.surface: A composer writes a piece while living in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Rubinstein's best-known piece is his Melody in F, a tune.

clue.text: One securing the door of its stable?

definitions.text: One securing the door of its stable?

parts.words: One securing the door of its stable?
parts.note: literally one who fastens a door with a bar, but recalls locking the stable door after the horse has run off

explanation.surface: A stable hand locks up the horse for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is shutting the stable door after the horse has fled; the answer is both a door-fastener and a runaway horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolter is a horse prone to running away, and literally someone who slides a bar to fasten a door.

clue.text: Worms having such significance only in an avian context ?

definitions.text: Worms having such significance only in an avian context ?

parts.words: Worms having such significance only in an avian context ?
parts.note: worms matter as food only to birds, so their significance is to do with what is eaten

explanation.surface: A naturalist muses on why worms matter only to birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietetic means relating to diet, and worms are part of the diet of birds, not of people.

clue.text: Loser of race comforted with" apples

definitions.text: Loser of race comforted with" apples

parts.words: Loser of race comforted with" apples
parts.note: the Greek huntress who lost a footrace after stopping to pick up three golden apples, echoing the Song of Songs' 'comfort me with apples'

explanation.surface: A beaten runner is consoled with some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atalanta lost her race to Hippomenes because she stooped for golden apples he dropped.

clue.text: Goodfellow's master knew, the power of Love-in-idleness

definitions.text: Goodfellow's master knew, the power of Love-in-idleness

parts.words: Goodfellow's master knew, the power of Love-in-idleness
parts.note: Robin Goodfellow is Puck, in A Midsummer Night's Dream, sent by the fairy king to fetch the flower love-in-idleness whose juice causes infatuation

explanation.surface: An employer understands how a lazy romance can take hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon, king of the fairies, is Puck's master and uses the pansy's juice to make Titania fall in love.

clue.text: Thus to inspect beds gives doctor an advantage

parts.note: an edge is an advantage, as in 'having the edge'

explanation.surface: A ward round of checking the beds puts the doctor one up.
explanation.walkthrough: The beds are riverbeds or seabeds, not hospital ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge is to scoop up the bottom of a river or sea to search or clear it, examining what lies on the bed.

clue.text: Like mummy, to whom he gave the fateful handkerchief

definitions.text: Like mummy, to whom he gave the fateful handkerchief

parts.words: Like mummy, to whom he gave the fateful handkerchief
parts.note: an embalmed body from the Nile and, in Othello, the charmer who gave the Moor's mother the handkerchief that later dooms Desdemona

explanation.surface: A mother receives a gift of a handkerchief that will bring disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mummy' looks like a mother but is also an embalmed body; Othello says 'That handkerchief did an Egyptian to my mother give'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mummies come from ancient Egypt, and in Othello the handkerchief was a charm from a woman of that land.
